objectives: Identify and document whether the attached dataset contains usable measures of weekly exercise, sleep quality, study year, and relevant student population information.

Develop at least two falsifiable, literature-informed hypotheses about the association between weekly exercise and sleep quality, including whether the association differs across study years, with each hypothesis tied to variables available in the dataset.

Lock an analysis plan that defines the population, variable construction, missing-data handling, statistical comparison or model, uncertainty reporting, and checks for differences across study years before examining results.

Execute the locked plan and produce traceable results that report the direction, magnitude, uncertainty, limitations, and any negative or inconclusive findings without implying causation beyond what the data support.
scope_in: University students represented in the attached dataset.
The association between weekly exercise and sleep quality.
Whether that association varies by study year.
Measurement quality, missingness, subgroup sizes, and confounding relevant to interpreting these associations.
scope_out: Causal claims that exercise improves sleep.
Populations not represented by the dataset.
Outcomes or exposures unrelated to exercise, sleep quality, or study year except when needed to assess confounding or data quality.
Post hoc changes to hypotheses, metrics, subgroup definitions, or success criteria based on observed results.
success_criteria: The dataset artifact documents usable definitions, coverage, and limitations for weekly exercise, sleep quality, and study year, or explicitly records that one or more cannot be measured.
The hypothesis artifact contains at least two falsifiable hypotheses, each naming dataset variables and an outcome, with literature support labeled separately from testability.

The experiment-design artifact contains a locked, reproducible plan specifying variable construction, missing-data rules, primary analysis, study-year comparison, uncertainty reporting, and integrity checks.

The execution artifact reports code-generated results with sample accounting, effect estimates or appropriate association measures, uncertainty, subgroup results, and limitations; supported, null, and inconclusive outcomes all count as successful completion when the plan was followed.
kill_criteria: The attached dataset cannot identify university students or cannot measure weekly exercise, sleep quality, or study year.
There is insufficient variation or usable data in the primary exposure, outcome, or study-year variable to test the question credibly.
The data structure or missingness makes the planned association and cross-year analyses uninterpretable, and no defensible alternative is available within scope.
The literature review yields no testable distinction beyond restating an established result, leaving no worthwhile hypothesis to evaluate in this dataset.
assumptions: The attached dataset is accessible to the dataset stage and contains at least some records relevant to university students.
The researcher wants an observational association study rather than a causal intervention evaluation.
Sleep quality and weekly exercise can be operationalized from the attached data if suitable fields exist; the dataset stage must verify this rather than assume it.
Study year is intended as a categorical or ordinal grouping variable, subject to the dataset's actual coding.

rationale: The case specifies an exploratory dataset question rather than a fixed claim, comparison, metric, and decision rule, so a confirmatory posture would be unjustified. The charter therefore prioritizes measurement verification, falsifiable hypotheses, a locked observational analysis, and transparent reporting across study years. No dataset or literature facts are asserted here because no dataset identifier or artifacts are available to verify; the dataset stage must establish what the attachment can actually measure. The scope excludes causal language to preserve fidelity to the apparent association question.

options_considered.summary: Pre-register one primary exercise–sleep comparison and a fixed study-year interaction test.
options_considered.why_not: The case does not specify a single claim, contrast, metric, or decision rule, and the intent is explore_dataset.

options_considered.summary: Allow a broad student-wellbeing analysis around exercise and sleep.
options_considered.why_not: This would invite drift beyond the stated exercise, sleep-quality, and study-year question.

evidence.point: The problem asks about weekly exercise, sleep quality, university students, and variation across study years.
The pipeline is before the dataset stage, with no artifacts or verified dataset identifier available.

assumptions: The attached dataset is accessible to the dataset stage and contains relevant student records.
would_change_my_mind: The researcher clarifies a fixed causal or comparative claim with a prespecified contrast, metric, and decision rule.
Dataset inspection shows that the attached data cannot measure one of the core variables or do not represent university students.
handoff: Verify the attached dataset's identity, access, license, provenance, and usable revision before designing hypotheses.
Inventory exact fields, coding, units, missingness, and sample sizes for exercise, sleep quality, study year, and student status.
Do not infer causation or invent proxies without clearly labeling and justifying them.
Report whether subgroup sizes and variable variation are sufficient for the study-year analysis; flag any kill criterion as a known risk.
brief: I recommend an exploratory observational charter focused narrowly on the association between weekly exercise and sleep quality and on variation across study years. The dataset stage must first verify that the attached data actually measure these concepts and have enough usable variation; null or inconclusive results will still satisfy the charter if the locked plan is followed. I have not added open questions because the research question is clear enough for the pipeline to begin.
